+        is_gated: bool = True,
+        workspace: LoraWorkspace | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        if not providers:
+            raise ValueError("a MoE LoRA runner needs at least one provider")
+        self.providers = dict(providers)
+        geometries = {
+            (
+                provider.hidden_size,
+                provider.intermediate_size,
+                provider.num_local_experts,
+                provider.gate_up_slices,
+                provider.contract.lora_delta_dtype,
+            )
+            for provider in self.providers.values()
+        }
+        if len(geometries) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("providers of one layer must share resident geometry")
+        (
+            self.hidden_size,
+            self.intermediate_size,
+            self.num_local_experts,
+            self.gate_up_slices,
+            self.lora_delta_dtype,
+        ) = next(iter(geometries))
+        self.top_k = top_k
+        self.routed_scaling_factor = routed_scaling_factor
+        self.activation = activation
+        self.is_gated = is_gated
+        self.workspace = workspace if workspace is not None else LoraWorkspace()
+        self.plans: dict[Phase, SelectedPlan] = {}
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_layer(
+        cls,
+        base_layer: FusedMoE,
+        *,
+        workspace: LoraWorkspace | None = None,
+        is_shared_outer: bool,
+        physical_rank: int,
+    ) -> MoeLoraRunner:
+        family = cls._admit(base_layer)
+        weight_device = base_layer.w2_weight.device
+        if weight_device.type != "cuda":
+            raise NotImplementedError("MoE LoRA requires a CUDA layer")
+        major, _ = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(weight_device)
+        architecture = architecture_for_capability(major)
+        config = base_layer.moe_runner_config
+        activation = ActivationFn.parse(config.activation)
+        plans = resolve_plans(
+            architecture=architecture,
+            is_shared_outer=is_shared_outer,
+            physical_rank=physical_rank,
+            activation=activation,
+            hidden_size=int(base_layer.hidden_size),
+            num_local_experts=int(base_layer.num_local_experts),
+            quant_family=family,
+        )
+        # Shared finalizers hold the rank reduction in one tile, tested up to 256.
+        if physical_rank > 256 and any(
+            sel.plan.finalize.family is not FinalizeFamily.MATERIALIZED
+            for sel in plans.values()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"the shared finalizes are capped at rank 256, got {physical_rank}"
+            )
+        vendor = get_moe_runner_backend().value.removeprefix("lora_")
+        runner = cls(
+            providers={
+                rows: cls._build_provider(
+                    base_layer, base_gemm_rows=rows, vendor=vendor, family=family
+                )
+                for rows in dict.fromkeys(sel.base_gemm_rows for sel in plans.values())
+            },
+            top_k=int(config.top_k),
+            routed_scaling_factor=config.routed_scaling_factor,
+            activation=activation,
+            is_gated=bool(config.is_gated),
+            workspace=workspace,
+        )
+        for sel in plans.values():
+            runner.validate_plan(sel.plan, base_gemm_rows=sel.base_gemm_rows)
+        runner.plans = dict(plans)
+        return runner
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _weight_family(base_layer: FusedMoE) -> str:
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.unquant import UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod
+
+        quant_method = base_layer.quant_method
+        if isinstance(quant_method, UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod):
+            if (
+                base_layer.w13_weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+                or base_layer.w2_weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+            ):
+                raise NotImplementedError(
+                    "MoE LoRA on an unquantized layer requires resident BF16 weights"
+                )
+            return "bf16"
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8 import Fp8MoEMethod
+
+        if isinstance(quant_method, Fp8MoEMethod):
+            if base_layer.params_dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+                raise NotImplementedError("FP8 MoE LoRA requires BF16 activations.")
+            if not quant_method.block_quant or getattr(
+                quant_method, "use_mxfp8", False
+            ):
+                raise NotImplementedError(
+                    "MoE LoRA on FP8 requires 128-block weight quantization; "
+                    "per-tensor and MXFP8 layers are unsupported"
+                )
+            if base_layer.w13_weight.dtype != torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+                raise NotImplementedError(
+                    "MoE LoRA on FP8 requires resident float8_e4m3fn weights; "
+                    "a Marlin-repacked FP8 layer is unsupported"
+                )
+            return "fp8"
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import (
+            ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod,
+        )
+
+        if isinstance(quant_method, ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod):
+            return "nvfp4"
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            "MoE LoRA supports unquantized BF16, 128-block FP8, and NVFP4 "
+            f"MoE; this layer's quant method is {type(quant_method).__name__}"
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _admit(cls, base_layer: FusedMoE) -> str:
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher.standard import StandardDispatcher
+
+        family = cls._weight_family(base_layer)
+        if not isinstance(base_layer.dispatcher, StandardDispatcher):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "MoE LoRA currently requires the Standard dispatcher"
+            )
+
+        major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()
+        if major not in (9, 10):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"MoE LoRA supports SM90 and SM100 only; this device is "
+                f"sm{major}{minor}. Its base GEMMs are WGMMA (SM90) and "
+                "tcgen05 (SM100) kernels, and no other architecture implements "
+                "either -- SM120 included, despite reporting a higher major."
+            )
+        if base_layer.dispatcher.skip_local_expert_mapping:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "MoE LoRA requires EP-local expert IDs at the runner "
+                "boundary, but this dispatcher keeps global IDs"
+            )
+        if base_layer.should_fuse_routed_scaling_factor_in_topk:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "MoE LoRA applies routed scaling exactly once in its own "
+                "finalize; this layer already folds it into the top-k weights. "
+                "Under a lora backend only ModelOpt NVFP4 does that, so those "
+                "experts need --moe-runner-backend lora_marlin"
+            )
+        if getattr(base_layer, "with_bias", False):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "MoE LoRA providers carry no expert biases; this layer has them"
+            )
+
+        config = base_layer.moe_runner_config
+        # Membership by value: `str in Enum` raises TypeError before Python 3.12.
+        supported_activation = config.activation in {fn.value for fn in ActivationFn}
+        if (
+            not supported_activation
+            or config.gemm1_alpha is not None
+            or config.gemm1_clamp_limit is not None
+            or config.swiglu_limit is not None
+            or config.apply_router_weight_on_input
+            or config.no_combine
+            or config.num_fused_shared_experts
+        ):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "MoE LoRA supports SiLU or ReLU2 (gated or not) without "
+                "fused shared experts, with route weighting owned by finalize"
+            )
+        return family
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _build_provider(
+        base_layer: FusedMoE,
+        *,
+        base_gemm_rows: str,
+        vendor: str,
+        family: str,
+    ) -> MoeBaseProvider:
+        provider_cls = select_provider_cls(base_gemm_rows, family, vendor)
+        quant_info = provider_cls.contract.quant_info_cls.from_layer(base_layer)
+        return provider_cls(quant_info)
+
+    def validate_plan(self, plan: MoePlan, *, base_gemm_rows: str) -> None:
+        provider = self.providers[base_gemm_rows]
+        if plan.act.activation is not self.activation:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"plan activation {plan.act.activation.value} does not match "
+                f"resident layer activation {self.activation.value}"
+            )
+        expected_slices = 2 if self.is_gated else 1
+        if provider.gate_up_slices != expected_slices:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"provider exposes {provider.gate_up_slices} gate/up slices "
+                f"but is_gated={self.is_gated} needs {expected_slices}"
+            )
+
+    def run(
+        self,
+        dispatch_output: StandardDispatchOutput,
+        batch: MoeLoraBatch,
+    ) -> StandardCombineInput:
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher.standard import StandardCombineInput
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import TopKOutputChecker
+
+        phase = Phase.PREFILL if batch.is_prefill else Phase.DECODE
+        selected = self.plans[phase]
+        launch_config = selected.tiles.config_for(
+            dispatch_output.hidden_states.shape[0]
+        )
+
+        provider = self.providers[selected.base_gemm_rows]
+        hidden_states = dispatch_output.hidden_states
+        topk_output = dispatch_output.topk_output
+        assert TopKOutputChecker.format_is_standard(topk_output)
+        topk_ids = topk_output.topk_ids
+
+        num_tokens = hidden_states.shape[0]
+        if (
+            batch.token_lora_mapping.ndim != 1
+            or batch.token_lora_mapping.shape[0] != num_tokens
+        ):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "MoE LoRA token/adapter assignment does not match the MoE "
+                f"token domain: mapping has {batch.token_lora_mapping.shape[0]} rows "
+                f"but the runner received {num_tokens}. Gather/remap "
+                "assignments before MoE-DP execution."
+            )
+
+        self.workspace.begin_forward(
+            graph_mode=batch.use_cuda_graph, is_prefill_graph=batch.is_prefill
+        )
+        routes = build_moe_routes(
+            selected.plan,
+            topk_ids=topk_ids,
+            token_lora_mapping=batch.token_lora_mapping,
+            num_local_experts=self.num_local_experts,
+            max_loras=batch.max_loras,
+            block_size=launch_config.routing_block_size,
+            workspace=self.workspace,
+        )
+
+        gate_up, base_gemm_state, gateup_out = self._run_gate_up(
+            selected.plan,
+            launch_config,
+            provider,
+            routes,
+            hidden_states,
+            topk_ids,
+            batch,
+            num_tokens,
+        )
+        act_out, down_a_input, down_a_gather = self._run_act(
+            selected.plan,
+            launch_config,
+            provider,
+            routes,
+            base_gemm_state,
+            gateup_out,
+            gate_up,
+            topk_ids,
+            batch,
+            num_tokens,
+        )
+        output = self._allocate_output(
+            num_tokens=num_tokens,
+            dtype=hidden_states.dtype,
+            device=act_out.device,
+        )
+        down_out, down_rank, down_delta = self._run_down(
+            selected.plan,
+            launch_config,
+            provider,
+            routes,
+            base_gemm_state,
+            act_out,
+            down_a_input,
+            down_a_gather,
+            batch,
+        )
+        output = self._run_finalize(
+            selected.plan,
+            launch_config,
+            provider,
+            routes,
+            base_gemm_state,
+            output,
+            down_out,
+            down_rank,
+            down_delta,
+            topk_output,
+            batch,
+            num_tokens,
+        )
+        return StandardCombineInput(hidden_states=output)
+
+    def _run_a(
+        self,
+        launch_config: MoeLoraLaunchConfig,
+        spec: ASpec,
+        input: torch.Tensor,
+        weight: torch.Tensor,
+        routes: MoeLoraRoutes,
+        name: str,
+        *,
+        pair_to_row: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if spec.family is AFamily.TOKEN_GROUPED:
+            route = routes.shared_token
+            if route is None:
+                raise ValueError("shared token route was not constructed")
+        elif spec.family in (AFamily.PER_ROW, AFamily.TOKEN_DENSE):
+            route = routes.raw(spec.is_shared_outer)
+        else:
+            route = routes.aligned(spec.is_shared_outer)
+        num_output_rows = (
+            route.num_tokens
+            if spec.output_layout is BridgeLayout.TOKEN_MAJOR
+            else route.num_rows
+        )
+        shape: tuple[int, ...] = (num_output_rows, weight.shape[1])
+        if spec.family is AFamily.TOKEN_DENSE:
+            # One bridge plane per resident slot; per-row B indexes the planes.
+            shape = (route.max_loras, num_output_rows, weight.shape[1])
+        output = self.workspace.tensor(
+            f"{name}:output",
+            shape,
+            dtype=self.lora_delta_dtype,
+            device=input.device,
+        )
+        config = launch_config.for_a(spec.site)
+        pair_input = spec.site is Site.DOWN
+        match spec.family.value:
+            case "token_grouped":
+                grouped_lora_a(input, weight, output, route, config=config)
+            case "grouped":
+                partial = counters = None
+                split_k = int(config.get("SPLIT_K", 1))
+                if split_k > 1:
+                    # Serial split-K: the last arrival sums the FP32 planes and
+                    # resets its counter for the next graph replay.
+                    partial = self.workspace.tensor(
+                        f"{name}:partial",
+                        (split_k, num_output_rows, weight.shape[1]),
+                        dtype=torch.float32,
+                        device=input.device,
+                    )
+                    tiles = (
+                        triton.cdiv(route.sorted_pair_ids.numel(), route.block_size)
+                        * shrink_column_tiles(
+                            int(config["BLOCK_SIZE_N"]), weight.shape[1], 1, False
+                        )[1]
+                    )
+                    counters = self.workspace.tensor(
+                        f"{name}:splitk_counters",
+                        (tiles,),
+                        dtype=torch.int32,
+                        device=input.device,
+                        zero_on_first_allocation=True,
+                    )
+                grouped_lora_a(
+                    input,
+                    weight,
+                    output,
+                    route,
+                    config=config,
+                    pair_input=pair_input,
+                    pair_to_row=pair_to_row,
+                    partial=partial,
+                    counters=counters,
+                )
+            case "per_row":
+                per_row_lora_a(
+                    input, weight, output, route, config=config, pair_input=pair_input
+                )
+            case "token_dense":
+                torch.matmul(
+                    input,
+                    weight.transpose(1, 2),
+                    out=output.view(weight.shape[0], input.shape[0], weight.shape[1]),
+                )
+            case family:
+                raise NotImplementedError(f"no LoRA-A executor for {family!r}")
+        return output
+
+    def _run_b(
+        self,
+        launch_config: MoeLoraLaunchConfig,
+        spec: BSpec,
+        bridge: torch.Tensor,
+        weight: torch.Tensor,
+        destination: torch.Tensor,
+        routes: MoeLoraRoutes,
+        *,
+        slot_planes: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        route = (
+            routes.raw(spec.is_shared_outer)
+            if spec.family is BFamily.PER_ROW
+            else routes.aligned(spec.is_shared_outer)
+        )
+        config = launch_config.for_b(spec.site)
+        if spec.site is Site.GATE_UP:
+            width = weight.shape[1] // self.gate_up_slices
+            offsets = tuple(slice_id * width for slice_id in range(self.gate_up_slices))
+        else:
+            offsets = (0,)
+        run_lora_b(
+            spec,
+            bridge=bridge,
+            weight=weight,
+            destination=destination,
+            routing=route,
+            destination_offsets=offsets,
+            config=config,
+            pair_bridge=spec.input_layout is BridgeLayout.PAIR_MAJOR,
+            slot_planes=slot_planes,
+        )
+
+    def _run_gate_up(
+        self,
+        plan: MoePlan,
+        launch_config: MoeLoraLaunchConfig,
+        provider: MoeBaseProvider,
+        routes: MoeLoraRoutes,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        batch: MoeLoraBatch,
+        num_tokens: int,
+    ) -> tuple[_LoraStageState, object, torch.Tensor]:
+        state = _LoraStageState()
+
+        def gate_up_a() -> None:
+            state.rank = self._run_a(
+                launch_config,
+                plan.gate_up_a,
+                hidden_states,
+                batch.gate_up_lora_a.flatten(0, 1),
+                routes,
+                "gate_up_a",
+            )
+
+        def gate_up_b() -> None:
+            delta = self.workspace.tensor(
+                "gate_up_b:delta",
+                (
+                    num_tokens * self.top_k,
+                    self.gate_up_slices * self.intermediate_size,
+                ),
+                dtype=self.lora_delta_dtype,
+                device=state.rank.device,
+            )
+            self._run_b(
+                launch_config,
+                plan.gate_up_b,
+                state.rank,
+                batch.gate_up_lora_b.flatten(0, 1),
+                delta,
+                routes,
+                slot_planes=plan.gate_up_a.family is AFamily.TOKEN_DENSE,
+            )
+            state.delta = delta
+
+        def base() -> tuple[object, torch.Tensor]:
+            base_gemm_state = provider.prepare(
+                hidden_states,
+                topk_ids,
+                self.top_k,
+                self.workspace,
+            )
+            gateup_out = self.workspace.tensor(
+                "base:gateup",
+                provider.gateup_out_shape(base_gemm_state),
+                dtype=provider.contract.gate_up_output_dtype,
+                device=hidden_states.device,
+            )
+            provider.gateup(base_gemm_state, gateup_out)
+            provider.release_prepared_inputs(base_gemm_state)
+            return base_gemm_state, gateup_out
+
+        if plan.gate_up_overlap is GateUpOverlap.NONE:
+            gate_up_a()
+            if plan.gate_up_b is not None:
+                gate_up_b()
+            base_gemm_state, gateup = base()
+        elif plan.gate_up_overlap is GateUpOverlap.GATE_UP_A:
+            base_gemm_state, gateup = self.workspace.run_parallel(
+                name=plan.gate_up_overlap.value,
+                device=hidden_states.device,
+                compute=base,
+                side=gate_up_a,
+            )
+            if plan.gate_up_b is not None:
+                gate_up_b()
+        else:
+
+            def gate_up_a_b() -> None:
+                gate_up_a()
+                gate_up_b()
+
+            base_gemm_state, gateup = self.workspace.run_parallel(
+                name=plan.gate_up_overlap.value,
+                device=hidden_states.device,
+                compute=base,
+                side=gate_up_a_b,
+            )
+        return state, base_gemm_state, gateup
+
+    def _run_act(
+        self,
+        plan: MoePlan,
+        launch_config: MoeLoraLaunchConfig,
+        provider: MoeBaseProvider,
+        routes: MoeLoraRoutes,
+        base_gemm_state,
+        gateup_out: torch.Tensor,
+        gate_up: _LoraStageState,
+        topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        batch: MoeLoraBatch,
+        num_tokens: int,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
+        act_out = self.workspace.tensor(
+            "act:masked",
+            provider.act_out_shape(base_gemm_state),
+            dtype=provider.contract.lora_activation_dtype,
+            device=gateup_out.device,
+        )
+        provider_rows = act_out.view(-1, act_out.shape[-1])
+        pair_to_row = base_gemm_state.pair_to_row
+        # Fused B+activation can feed grouped down-A through the provider's row map.
+        exposes_pair_activation = not (
+            plan.act.family is ActFamily.B_ACTIVATION
+            and plan.down_a.family is AFamily.GROUPED
+        )
+        act_pairs = (
+            self.workspace.tensor(
+                "act:pairs",
+                (num_tokens, self.top_k, provider.intermediate_size),
+                dtype=provider.contract.lora_activation_dtype,
+                device=gateup_out.device,
+            )
+            if exposes_pair_activation
+            else None
+        )
+        if plan.act.family is ActFamily.MATERIALIZED:
+            quant_group = provider.contract.act_quant_group
+            act_quant = None
+            if quant_group is not None:
+                # Quantize during activation to avoid a separate down-GEMM input pass.
+                act_quant = (
+                    self.workspace.tensor(
+                        "act:quant_rows",
+                        act_out.shape,
+                        dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+                        device=gateup_out.device,
+                    ),
+                    self.workspace.tensor(
+                        "act:quant_scales",
+                        (act_out.shape[0], act_out.shape[1] // quant_group),
+                        dtype=torch.float32,
+                        device=gateup_out.device,
+                    ),
+                )
+            provider.act_with_delta(
+                base_gemm_state,
+                gateup_out,
+                gate_up.delta.view(
+                    num_tokens,
+                    self.top_k,
+                    provider.gate_up_slices * provider.intermediate_size,
+                ),
+                topk_ids,
+                act_out,
+                act_pairs,
+                activation=self.activation.value,
+                **({"act_quant": act_quant} if act_quant is not None else {}),
+            )
+            # Pair-major input needs no gather.
+            return act_out, act_pairs, None
+
+        provider.fused_act(
+            base_gemm_state,
+            activation=self.activation.value,
+            base_gateup=gateup_out,
+            act_rows=act_out,
+            act_pairs=act_pairs,
+            routing=routes.aligned(False),
+            config=launch_config.for_act(plan.act.family),
+            bridge_gateup=gate_up.rank,
+            b_gate_up=batch.gate_up_lora_b.flatten(0, 1),
+            bridge_top_k=(
+                self.top_k
+                if plan.gate_up_a.output_layout is BridgeLayout.TOKEN_MAJOR
+                else 1
+            ),
+        )
+        if exposes_pair_activation:
+            return act_out, act_pairs, None
+        # Only provider-ordered input uses pair_to_row; pair-major input must not.
+        return act_out, provider_rows, pair_to_row
+
+    def _run_down(
+        self,
+        plan: MoePlan,
+        launch_config: MoeLoraLaunchConfig,
+        provider: MoeBaseProvider,
+        routes: MoeLoraRoutes,
+        base_gemm_state,
+        act_out: torch.Tensor,
+        down_a_input: torch.Tensor,
+        down_a_gather: torch.Tensor | None,
+        batch: MoeLoraBatch,
+    ) -> tuple[
+        torch.Tensor,
+        torch.Tensor,
+        torch.Tensor | None,
+    ]:
+        state = _LoraStageState()
+
+        def down_a() -> None:
+            state.rank = self._run_a(
+                launch_config,
+                plan.down_a,
+                down_a_input.view(-1, self.intermediate_size),
+                batch.down_lora_a.flatten(0, 1),
+                routes,
+                "down_a",
+                pair_to_row=down_a_gather,
+            )
+
+        def down_b() -> None:
+            delta = self.workspace.tensor(
+                "down_b:delta",
+                (state.rank.shape[0], self.hidden_size),
+                dtype=self.lora_delta_dtype,
+                device=state.rank.device,
+            )
+            self._run_b(
+                launch_config,
+                plan.down_b,
+                state.rank,
+                batch.down_lora_b.flatten(0, 1),
+                delta,
+                routes,
+            )
+            state.delta = delta

+        def down_b_into_base(down_out: torch.Tensor) -> None:

+from __future__ import annotations

+import torch

+from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.sm120_nvfp4_moe import _transpose_module

+class Nvfp4LayoutCycle:
+    """Own the two views of a fixed, serial set of [512,1024,1344] weights."""
+
+    def __init__(self, weights):
+        if not weights:
+            raise ValueError("A layout cycle requires at least one expert weight")
+        first = weights[0]
+        if first.device.type != "cuda":
+            raise ValueError("The layout cycle requires CUDA weights")
+        for weight in weights:
+            if (
+                weight.shape != (512, 1024, 1344)
+                or weight.dtype != torch.uint8
+                or not weight.is_contiguous()
+                or weight.device != first.device
+            ):
+                raise ValueError("Incompatible NVFP4 FC2 weight layout")
+        if len({weight.data_ptr() for weight in weights}) != len(weights):
+            raise ValueError("Expert weights in a layout cycle must not alias")
+        self.original = tuple(weights)
+        self.scratch = None
+        self.pair = ()
+        self.is_pair = False
+        # Compile before any graph capture can reach the state transition.
+        self._forward = _transpose_module(1024, 1344)
+        self._inverse = _transpose_module(1344, 1024)
+
+    def prepare_workspace(self):
+        if self.scratch is not None:
+            return
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            raise RuntimeError("NVFP4 workspace must be prepared before graph capture")
+        # Allocate from runtime headroom, not before Mamba/KV pool sizing, where it
+        # would count as weights and could leave the state pool under one request.
+        self.scratch = torch.empty_like(self.original[0])
+        self.pair = tuple(
+            weight.view(512, 1344, 1024)
+            for weight in (self.scratch, *self.original[:-1])
+        )
+
+    def ensure(self, pair: bool):
+        if pair == self.is_pair:
+            return
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            raise RuntimeError("NVFP4 layout transitions must run before graph capture")
+        if pair:
+            self.prepare_workspace()
+            for original, paired in zip(self.original, self.pair):
+                self._forward.run(original, paired)
+        else:
+            for original, paired in reversed(tuple(zip(self.original, self.pair))):
+                self._inverse.run(paired, original)
+        self.is_pair = pair

+#!/bin/bash
+# Build the sgl-flash-mla wheel inside a CUDA-versioned container.
+#
+# Usage: build_sgl_flash_mla.sh <PYTHON_VERSION> <CUDA_VERSION> <FLASHMLA_SRC> [ARCH]
+#   PYTHON_VERSION: e.g. 3.12 -- only picks the interpreter that drives the build.
+#                   The wheel is abi3 and serves CPython 3.10+ whichever is used.
+#   CUDA_VERSION:   13.4
+#   FLASHMLA_SRC:   path to a checkout of sgl-project/FlashMLA (submodules included)
+#   ARCH:           x86_64 (default) or aarch64
+#
+# Writes:
+#   <FLASHMLA_SRC>/dist/      — wheel tagged +cu130 and manylinux2014
+#   <FLASHMLA_SRC>/dist-pypi/ — the same wheel with +cu130 stripped
+#                               (PyPI rejects local-version segments)
+#
+# On the two version numbers: the kernels are compiled by CUDA 13.4, because they
+# use `cvt` with `.scaled::n2::ue8m0` (nvcc >= 13.1) and older toolkits emit
+# suboptimal instructions for them. The +cu130 tag describes the *runtime* the
+# wheel is published for: the extensions link libcudart.so.13, whose SONAME
+# carries only the major version, and call no cudart API newer than 13.0, so a
+# 13.4-built wheel loads against the cu130 torch SGLang ships.
+set -ex
+
+if [ $# -lt 3 ]; then
+  echo "Usage: $0 <PYTHON_VERSION> <CUDA_VERSION> <FLASHMLA_SRC> [ARCH]"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+PYTHON_VERSION="$1"
+CUDA_VERSION="$2"
+FLASHMLA_SRC="$(cd "$3" && pwd)"
+ARCH="${4:-$(uname -i)}"
+
+case "${CUDA_VERSION}" in
+  13.4) CU_TAG=cu130 ;;
+  *)
+    echo "Unsupported CUDA_VERSION: ${CUDA_VERSION} (the kernels require 13.4)" >&2
+    exit 1
+    ;;
+esac
+
+if [ "${ARCH}" = "aarch64" ]; then
+  BASE_IMG="pytorch/manylinuxaarch64-builder"
+else
+  BASE_IMG="pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder"
+fi
+
+PY_TAG="cp${PYTHON_VERSION//.}-cp${PYTHON_VERSION//.}"
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
+DOCKERFILE="${REPO_ROOT}/docker/sgl-flash-mla.Dockerfile"
+RENAME_SCRIPT="${SCRIPT_DIR}/rename_sgl_flash_mla_whl.sh"
+
+DEPS_TAG="sgl-flash-mla-deps:cuda${CUDA_VERSION}-${PY_TAG}-${ARCH}"
+
+echo "----------------------------------------"
+echo "PYTHON_VERSION: ${PYTHON_VERSION}"
+echo "CUDA_VERSION:   ${CUDA_VERSION}"
+echo "CU_TAG:         ${CU_TAG}"
+echo "ARCH:           ${ARCH}"
+echo "BASE_IMG:       ${BASE_IMG}"
+echo "FLASHMLA_SRC:   ${FLASHMLA_SRC}"
+echo "----------------------------------------"
+
+docker build \
+  -f "${DOCKERFILE}" "$(dirname "${DOCKERFILE}")" \
+  --build-arg BASE_IMG="${BASE_IMG}" \
+  --build-arg CUDA_VERSION="${CUDA_VERSION}" \
+  --build-arg ARCH="${ARCH}" \
+  --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION="${PYTHON_VERSION}" \
+  --build-arg PYTHON_TAG="${PY_TAG}" \
+  -t "${DEPS_TAG}" \
+  --network=host
+
+mkdir -p "${FLASHMLA_SRC}/dist"
+
+# 1) Build. --no-build-isolation because setup.py imports torch, which the image
+#    provides; FlashMLA declares no PEP 518 build requirements.
+#    NVCC_THREADS defaults to 32 in setup.py; MAX_JOBS is what actually
+#    parallelises, and without ninja on PATH torch silently ignores it.
+docker run --rm \
+  --network=host \
+  -v "${FLASHMLA_SRC}:/flashmla" \
+  -w /flashmla \
+  -e MAX_JOBS="${MAX_JOBS:-$(nproc)}" \
+  "${DEPS_TAG}" \
+  bash -c 'set -eux; python3 setup.py bdist_wheel'
+

+
+This is an NPU CI helper: it imports the shared multimodal_gen runner
+READ-ONLY. The shard composition must match what
+``python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py`` would execute, so the LPT
+assignment is reused instead of reimplemented, but no platform-shared test
+code is modified.

+    <workspace>/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/test_server_1_npu.py::TestDiffusionServerOneNpu::test_diffusion_generation[ernie_image_t2i_1npu]

+coverage directory name and test_selector.py recovers the repo-relative test
+path from the ``__sglang__sglang__`` workspace marker.

+    python3 list_multimodal_tests.py --suite 1-npu \
+        --partition-id 0 --total-partitions 2 -o /tmp/selected_tests.txt

+import argparse
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path

+SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+REPO_ROOT = SCRIPT_DIR.parents[3]

+# even when the package is not installed in editable mode.
+sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "python"))

+from sglang.multimodal_gen.test.runner import (  # noqa: E402
+    diffusion_suite_runner as runner,

+from sglang.multimodal_gen.test.runner.pytest_runner import (  # noqa: E402
+    collect_test_items,
+    partition_items_by_index,
+)
+
+
+def _case_files(suite: str, server_dir: Path) -> dict:
+    """Map case id -> absolute test file for a parametrized diffusion suite."""
+    mapping = {}
+    for filename, case_group in runner.PARAMETRIZED_CASE_GROUPS.get(suite, []):
+        file_path = server_dir / filename
+        for case in case_group:
+            mapping[case.id] = file_path
+    return mapping
+
+
+def _node_targets(file_path: Path, case_ids: list) -> list:
+    """Expand case ids into absolute pytest node-id targets for one file."""
+    filter_expr = " or ".join(f"[{case_id}]" for case_id in case_ids)
+    targets = []
+    for item in collect_test_items([str(file_path)], filter_expr):
+        # collect_test_items reports node ids relative to pytest's rootdir,
+        # which is not the checkout root. Rebuild them from the absolute file
+        # so the coverage collector can encode the workspace layout.
+        node = item.partition("::")[2]

+    return targets
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--suite", required=True, help="Diffusion suite, e.g. 1-npu")
+    parser.add_argument("--partition-id", type=int, default=0)
+    parser.add_argument("--total-partitions", type=int, default=1)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "-o",
+        "--output",
+        required=True,
+        help="Write the pytest targets (one per line) to this file.",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    test_root = Path(runner.__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+    server_dir = test_root / "server"
+
+    if args.suite in runner.PARAMETRIZED_CASE_GROUPS:
+        assignment = runner.build_local_partition_assignment(
+            args.suite, args.partition_id, args.total_partitions
+        )
+        case_files = _case_files(args.suite, server_dir)
+        missing = [cid for cid in assignment.case_ids if cid not in case_files]
+        if missing:
+            print(f"::warning::Cases absent from the {args.suite} config: {missing}")
+
+        targets = []
+        for file_path in sorted(
+            {case_files[cid] for cid in assignment.case_ids if cid in case_files}
+        ):
+            case_ids = [
+                cid for cid in assignment.case_ids if case_files.get(cid) == file_path
+            ]
+            targets.extend(_node_targets(file_path, case_ids))
+        for standalone_rel in assignment.standalone_files:
+            targets.append(str(server_dir / standalone_rel))
+    elif args.suite in runner.FILE_SUITES:
+        files = [str(server_dir / rel) for rel in runner.FILE_SUITES[args.suite]]
+        targets = partition_items_by_index(
+            files, args.partition_id, args.total_partitions
+        )
+    else:
+        parser.error(f"Unknown diffusion suite: {args.suite!r}")
+
+    unique_targets = []
+    seen = set()
+    for target in targets:
+        if target not in seen:
+            seen.add(target)
+            unique_targets.append(target)
+
+    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        for target in unique_targets:
+            f.write(target + "\n")
+
+    print(f"Listed {len(unique_targets)} test target(s) to {args.output}:")
+    for target in unique_targets:
+        print(f"  - {target}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Check that Dockerfiles building pinned wheels from source use the pinned versions.
+
+docker/Dockerfile.cu134 builds sgl-deep-gemm and sgl-deep-ep from source, strips
+their pins from python/pyproject.toml and installs the wheels with --no-deps, so a
+pin bump that misses the Dockerfile ships the old version without any install error.
+Every Dockerfile under docker/ that sets a default for one of the ARGs below is
+checked, so a renamed or newly added CUDA-specific Dockerfile stays covered.
+"""
+
+import glob
+import re
+import sys
+import tomllib
+from collections import defaultdict
+
+PYPROJECT = "python/pyproject.toml"
+
+# Package pinned in pyproject -> {Dockerfile ARG: prefix}; pin X needs ARG=<prefix>X.
+PINNED_ARGS = {
+    "sgl-deep-gemm": {"DEEPGEMM_REF": "v", "SGL_DEEP_GEMM_VERSION": ""},
+    "sgl-deep-ep": {"SGL_DEEP_EP_VERSION": ""},
+}
+
+# `package==X`: the Dockerfiles sed-replace this exact line, so no other form counts.
+_EXACT_PIN = re.compile(r"([\w.-]+)==(\S+)")
+# `ARG NAME=default`, possibly indented.
+_ARG_DEFAULT = re.compile(r"^\s*ARG\s+(\w+)=(.*)$", re.MULTILINE)
+
+
+def arg_defaults() -> dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]]:
+    """ARG name -> (path, default) for every ``ARG NAME=default`` under docker/."""
+    defaults = defaultdict(list)
+    for path in sorted(glob.glob("docker/**/*Dockerfile*", recursive=True)):
+        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
+            for name, value in _ARG_DEFAULT.findall(f.read()):
+                defaults[name].append((path, value.strip()))
+    return defaults
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    with open(PYPROJECT, "rb") as f:
+        deps = tomllib.load(f)["project"]["dependencies"]
+    pins = defaultdict(list)  # package -> X of every `package==X` dependency
+    for dep in deps:
+        match = _EXACT_PIN.fullmatch(dep)
+        if match:
+            pins[match.group(1)].append(match.group(2))
+    defaults = arg_defaults()
+
+    errors = []
+    for package, args in PINNED_ARGS.items():
+        if len(pins[package]) != 1:
+            errors.append(f"{PYPROJECT}: expected one exact '{package}==X' pin")
+            continue
+        version = pins[package][0]
+        for arg, prefix in args.items():
+            if not defaults[arg]:
+                errors.append(f"no Dockerfile sets ARG {arg}=...; this check is dead")
+            for path, value in defaults[arg]:
+                if value != prefix + version:
+                    errors.append(
+                        f"{path}: ARG {arg}={value}, expected {prefix}{version} "
+                        f"to match {package}=={version} in {PYPROJECT}"
+                    )
+
+    for error in errors:
+        print(f"ERROR: {error}")
+    return 1 if errors else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Retag a freshly-built sgl-flash-mla wheel for the sgl-whl index.
+#
+# setuptools tags the extension wheel `cp310-abi3-linux_x86_64`. `linux_x86_64`
+# is not installable from an index -- pip and PyPI both reject it -- so the
+# platform becomes manylinux2014_<arch>, and the version gains the +cuXXX local
+# segment the index keys on.
+#
+# The abi3 tag is left alone: the extensions register through
+# STABLE_TORCH_LIBRARY and need no CPython API beyond the Limited API, so one
+# wheel really does serve CPython 3.10+.
+#
+# Input:  dist/sgl_flash_mla-<VERSION>-cp310-abi3-linux_<ARCH>.whl
+# Output: dist/sgl_flash_mla-<VERSION>+<CU_TAG>-cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_<ARCH>.whl
+#
+# Usage: rename_sgl_flash_mla_whl.sh <WHEEL_DIR> <CU_TAG> <ARCH>
+set -ex
+
+if [ $# -lt 3 ]; then
+  echo "Usage: $0 <WHEEL_DIR> <CU_TAG> <ARCH>"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+WHEEL_DIR="$1"
+CU_TAG="$2"
+ARCH="$3"
+PLAT_TAG="manylinux2014_${ARCH}"
+
+PYTHON="${PYTHON:-python3}"
+"${PYTHON}" -m pip install --quiet wheel
+
+shopt -s nullglob
+wheel_files=("${WHEEL_DIR}"/sgl_flash_mla-*.whl)
+if [ ${#wheel_files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "No sgl_flash_mla wheel found under ${WHEEL_DIR}" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+for wheel in "${wheel_files[@]}"; do
+  TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
+  trap 'rm -rf -- "$TMPDIR"' ERR
+
+  "${PYTHON}" -m wheel unpack "$wheel" --dest "$TMPDIR"
+  UNPACKED=$(find "$TMPDIR" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d | head -1)
+  DIST_INFO=$(find "$UNPACKED" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "*.dist-info" | head -1)
+  WHEEL_META="${DIST_INFO}/WHEEL"
+  METADATA_FILE="${DIST_INFO}/METADATA"
+
+  # Only the platform part of the tag changes; the interpreter/ABI part stays abi3.
+  sed -i -E "s/^(Tag: [^-]+-[^-]+)-linux_${ARCH}$/\1-${PLAT_TAG}/" "$WHEEL_META"
+  grep -q "^Tag: .*-${PLAT_TAG}$" "$WHEEL_META" || {
+    echo "Failed to retag ${wheel}; WHEEL says:" >&2
+    cat "$WHEEL_META" >&2
+    exit 1
+  }
+
+  ORIG_VERSION=$(grep '^Version:' "$METADATA_FILE" | head -1 | sed 's/^Version:[[:space:]]*//')
+  if [[ "$ORIG_VERSION" == *"+${CU_TAG}"* ]]; then
+    NEW_VERSION="$ORIG_VERSION"
+  else
+    NEW_VERSION="${ORIG_VERSION}+${CU_TAG}"
+    sed -i "s/^Version:.*/Version: ${NEW_VERSION}/" "$METADATA_FILE"
+    OLD_BASE=$(basename "$DIST_INFO")
+    NEW_BASE="${OLD_BASE/${ORIG_VERSION}/${NEW_VERSION}}"
+    mv "$DIST_INFO" "${UNPACKED}/${NEW_BASE}"
+  fi
+
+  rm -f "$wheel"
+  "${PYTHON}" -m wheel pack "$UNPACKED" --dest-dir "$WHEEL_DIR"
+  rm -rf "$TMPDIR"
+  trap - ERR
+done
+
+echo "Renamed wheels in ${WHEEL_DIR}:"
+ls -lh "${WHEEL_DIR}"/*.whl

+        self.cp_size = cp_size
+        self.kv_calls = []
+
+    def materialize_full_kv(self, forward_batch, layer, k, v, swa_loc=None):
+        self.kv_calls.append((tuple(k.shape), tuple(v.shape)))
+
+
+def _cp_batch(out_cache_loc):
+    return SimpleNamespace(out_cache_loc=out_cache_loc, encoder_out_cache_loc=None)
+
+
+def _attn_layer():
+    return SimpleNamespace(is_cross_attention=False, k_scale=None, v_scale=None)
+
+
+def _fia_layer():
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        tp_q_head_num=16,
+        tp_k_head_num=8,
+        tp_v_head_num=8,
+        qk_head_dim=128,
+        v_head_dim=128,
+        scaling=0.08838834764831845,

+    """`_cp_allgather_and_save_kv_npu` must use the CP v2 strategy API."""
+

+class TestDoCpAttnFia(unittest.TestCase):
+    """`do_cp_attn_fia` delegates CP slicing to the strategy and only supplies FIA.
+
+    The ZigzagCPStrategy.run_attention owns prev/next slicing, concatenation and
+    pad-row re-appending; the backend's job is to hand it an FIA computation
+    closure and translate the strategy's cu_seqlens / KV-length tensors into the
+    lists FIA expects.
+    """

+    PHYSICAL_ROWS = 4
+
+    def setUp(self):

+        self.backend.page_size = 128

+        self.v_cache = torch.zeros(2163 * 128, 8 * 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def _fia(self, query, key, value, **kwargs):
+        record = dict(kwargs)
+        record["query"] = query
+        self.calls.append(record)
+        return (
+            torch.zeros(query.shape[0], query.shape[1], 128, dtype=query.dtype),
+            None,
+        )

+    def _meta(self, prev, next_len):
+        # single-batch CP metadata with the tensor fields run_attention reads
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            total_q_prev_tokens=prev,
+            total_q_next_tokens=next_len,

+        self.assertEqual(self.calls[1]["actual_seq_lengths_kv"], [3])

+    def test_output_keeps_physical_row_count(self):

+        self.assertEqual(self.calls[1]["query"].shape[0], 2)
+

+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Compare packed SwiGLU + FP8 quantization with its standalone fusion.
+
+Run on an idle GPU, e.g. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 python this_file.py
+--output-json logs/swiglu-fp8.json. CUDA graph timing excludes Python overhead.
+Each case measures both the producer alone and producer + unchanged FP8 GEMM.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+import triton
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import (
+    fp8_rowwise,
+    fused_packed_silu_mul_bitexact,
+    fused_packed_swiglu_fp8_rowwise,
+)
+
+
+def benchmark(rows, hidden, rounds, rep_ms):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    storage = torch.randn((1, rows, 3 * hidden), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    packed = storage[..., hidden:]
+    weights, weight_scales = fp8_rowwise(
+        torch.randn((3072, hidden), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16), 16
+    )
+
+    def separate():
+        values = fused_packed_silu_mul_bitexact(packed)
+        return fp8_rowwise(values.reshape(rows, hidden), 16)
+
+    def fused():
+        return fused_packed_swiglu_fp8_rowwise(packed)
+
+    def gemm(producer):
+        q, scales = producer()
+        return torch._scaled_mm(
+            q,
+            weights.T,
+            scales[:, None],
+            weight_scales[None, :],
+            out_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            use_fast_accum=True,
+        )
+
+    q, scales = separate()
+    fq, fs = fused()
+    assert torch.equal(q.view(torch.uint8), fq.view(torch.uint8))
+    assert torch.equal(scales, fs)
+    assert torch.equal(gemm(separate), gemm(fused))
+    result = {
+        "rows": rows,
+        "hidden": hidden,
+        "input_row_stride": packed.stride(1),
+        "padded_rows": q.shape[0],
+        "bit_exact": True,
+    }
+    for name, a, b in [
+        ("producer", separate, fused),
+        ("with_gemm", lambda: gemm(separate), lambda: gemm(fused)),
+    ]:
+        for _ in range(10):
+            a()
+            b()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        samples = {"separate": [], "fused": []}
+        # Alternate order to reduce thermal/clock bias.
+        for i in range(rounds):
+            order = [("separate", a), ("fused", b)]
+            if i % 2:
+                order.reverse()
+            for key, fn in order:
+                samples[key].append(
+                    triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(fn, rep=rep_ms) * 1000
+                )
+        medians = {k: statistics.median(v) for k, v in samples.items()}
+        result[name] = {
+            "samples_us": samples,
+            "median_us": medians,
+            "speedup": medians["separate"] / medians["fused"],
+            "reduction_pct": 100 * (1 - medians["fused"] / medians["separate"]),
+        }
+    return result
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output-json", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=5)
+    parser.add_argument("--rep-ms", type=int, default=100)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.rounds <= 0 or args.rep_ms <= 0:
+        parser.error("rounds and rep-ms must be positive")
+    results = []
+    for rows, hidden in [
+        (1, 9216),
+        (32, 9216),
+        (340, 9216),
+        (2720, 9216),
+        (3173, 9216),
+        (3173, 3072),
+    ]:
+        r = benchmark(rows, hidden, args.rounds, args.rep_ms)
+        results.append(r)
+        print(json.dumps(r), flush=True)
+    if args.output_json:
+        args.output_json.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        args.output_json.write_text(
+            json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+                    "torch": torch.__version__,
+                    "triton": triton.__version__,
+                    "mode": "CUDA graph, no profiler",
+                    "rounds": args.rounds,
+                    "rep_ms": args.rep_ms,
+                    "results": results,
+                },
+                indent=2,
+            )
+            + "\n"
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""gfx1250 per-token/per-channel FP8 GEMM tile, and the linear method that uses it.
+
+The tile indexes its operands modulo M and N instead of masking the loads, and
+caps BLOCK_SIZE_K at 64 because FP8 ``tl.dot`` miscompiles above that on this
+target. Guards: ragged M and small N still match a dequantized reference,
+``gfx1250_fp8_scaled_mm_supported`` rejects the shapes the K loop cannot cover,
+an all-zero activation row quantizes to exact zeros, and ``Fp8LinearMethod``
+both reaches the tile for an online-quantized checkpoint, lays its weights out
+row-major, and stays off the tile when the kill switch is set.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.fp8_gfx1250 import (
+    gfx1250_fp8_scaled_mm,
+    gfx1250_fp8_scaled_mm_supported,
+    per_token_quant_fp8_gfx1250,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.quantization.fp8 import (
+    Fp8Config,
+    Fp8LinearMethod,
+)
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_gfx1250_supported
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=60, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+_FP8_MAX = torch.finfo(torch.float8_e4m3fn).max
+
+
+def _quantize_weight(w: torch.Tensor):
+    """Mirror Fp8LinearMethod's online path: [N, K] bf16 -> fp8 [K, N] + per-channel scale."""
+    scale = (w.float().abs().amax(dim=1) / _FP8_MAX).clamp(min=1e-12)
+    q = (w.float() / scale[:, None]).clamp(-_FP8_MAX, _FP8_MAX).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    return q, scale
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(is_gfx1250_supported(), "requires an AMD gfx1250 GPU")
+class TestFp8GemmGfx1250(CustomTestCase):
+    def _check(self, M: int, N: int, K: int, with_bias: bool):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        x = torch.randn(M, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        w = torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.02
+        bias = (
+            torch.randn(N, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) if with_bias else None
+        )
+
+        wq, w_scale = _quantize_weight(w)
+        xq, x_scale = per_token_quant_fp8_gfx1250(x)
+
+        out = gfx1250_fp8_scaled_mm(
+            xq, wq.t(), x_scale, w_scale, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16, bias=bias
+        )
+        # Reference dequantizes the same FP8 operands, so this isolates the
+        # tile from the quantization error it inherits.
+        ref = (xq.float() * x_scale[:, None]) @ (wq.float() * w_scale[:, None]).t()
+        if bias is not None:
+            ref = ref + bias.float()
+
+        self.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(out).all())
+        rel = ((out.float() - ref).abs().mean() / ref.abs().mean()).item()
+        self.assertLess(rel, 5e-3, f"M={M} N={N} K={K} bias={with_bias} rel={rel}")
+
+    def test_flux2_720p_shapes(self):
+        for M, N, K in (
+            (4112, 55296, 6144),
+            (4112, 6144, 24576),
+            (3600, 36864, 6144),
+            (512, 6144, 15360),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(M=M, N=N, K=K):
+                self._check(M, N, K, with_bias=False)
+
+    def test_ragged_and_small(self):
+        for M, N, K in ((65, 6144, 6144), (4111, 6144, 6144), (4113, 320, 6144)):
+            with self.subTest(M=M, N=N, K=K):
+                self._check(M, N, K, with_bias=True)
+
+    def test_unsupported_shapes_are_rejected(self):
+        self.assertFalse(gfx1250_fp8_scaled_mm_supported(M=32, N=6144, K=6144))
+        self.assertFalse(gfx1250_fp8_scaled_mm_supported(M=512, N=6144, K=6176))
+        self.assertFalse(gfx1250_fp8_scaled_mm_supported(M=512, N=100, K=6144))
+        self.assertTrue(gfx1250_fp8_scaled_mm_supported(M=512, N=6144, K=6144))
+
+    def test_zero_row_quantizes_to_zero(self):
+        x = torch.randn(8, 6144, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        x[3] = 0
+        q, scale = per_token_quant_fp8_gfx1250(x)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(scale).all())
+        self.assertTrue((q[3].float() == 0).all())
+        roundtrip = q.float() * scale[:, None]
+        rel = ((roundtrip - x.float()).abs().mean() / x.float().abs().mean()).item()
+        self.assertLess(rel, 0.05)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(is_gfx1250_supported(), "requires an AMD gfx1250 GPU")
+class TestFp8LinearMethodDispatchGfx1250(CustomTestCase):
+    """The seam this change moves: which GEMM an online-FP8 linear ends up on."""
+
+    def test_online_checkpoint_selects_the_tile_and_matches_bf16(self):
+        method = Fp8LinearMethod(Fp8Config())
+        self.assertTrue(method.use_gfx1250_triton_fp8)
+
+        M, N, K = 512, 6144, 6144
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        layer = torch.nn.Module()
+        w = torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.02
+        layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w, requires_grad=False)
+        layer.input_scale = None
+        method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+        # The tile wants [K, N] fp8 weights with one scale per output channel;
+        # a per-tensor scale here would mean the dispatch picked another path.
+        self.assertEqual(layer.weight.dtype, torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(layer.weight.shape), (K, N))
+        self.assertEqual(layer.weight_scale.numel(), N)
+        # Row-major, not the transposed view this would otherwise be. The
+        # tile's configs are tuned for this layout and it is worth 1.05-1.33x,
+        # so a refactor that drops the transpose is a silent regression.
+        self.assertTrue(
+            layer.weight.is_contiguous(),
+            f"weight must be row-major [K, N]; strides {layer.weight.stride()}",
+        )
+

+        out = method.apply(layer, x)
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(out.shape), (M, N))
+        self.assertEqual(out.dtype, torch.bfloat16)
+
+        ref = x.float() @ w.float().t()
+        rel = ((out.float() - ref).abs().mean() / ref.abs().mean()).item()
+        self.assertLess(rel, 0.05, f"FP8 linear drifted from the BF16 result: {rel}")

+"""Bit-exact FLUX 3 video VAE QKV RMSNorm + rotate-half RoPE."""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import (
+    can_use_flux3_video_qknorm_rope,
+    flux3_video_qknorm_rope,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.vaes.flux3_video_vae import (
+    _VIDEO_QKV_GATE,
+    Natten3D,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=20, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+
+_EPS = 1e-5
+
+
+def _rotate_half(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    x1, x2 = x.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    return torch.cat([-x2, x1], dim=-1)
+
+
+def _reference(qkv: torch.Tensor, cos: torch.Tensor, sin: torch.Tensor):
+    q, k, v = qkv.unbind(4)
+    q = F.rms_norm(q, (q.shape[-1],), eps=_EPS)
+    k = F.rms_norm(k, (k.shape[-1],), eps=_EPS)
+    q = q * cos + _rotate_half(q) * sin
+    k = k * cos + _rotate_half(k) * sin
+    return q, k, v
+
+
+def _tables(t, h, w, device):
+    # Same construction as RotaryPositionEmbedding3D, base 256, head dim 64.
+    chunk = 16
+    axis = 1.0 / (256.0 ** (torch.arange(0, chunk, 2, device=device).float() / chunk))
+    inv = torch.stack([axis, axis, axis, torch.zeros(chunk // 2, device=device)])
+    grids = torch.meshgrid(
+        torch.arange(t, device=device, dtype=torch.float32),
+        torch.arange(h, device=device, dtype=torch.float32),
+        torch.arange(w, device=device, dtype=torch.float32),
+        indexing="ij",
+    )
+    pos = torch.stack(grids + (torch.zeros_like(grids[0]),), dim=-1)
+    freqs = torch.einsum("...a,af->...af", pos, inv.float()).reshape(1, t, h, w, 1, -1)
+    freqs = torch.cat([freqs, freqs], dim=-1)
+    return freqs.cos().bfloat16().contiguous(), freqs.sin().bfloat16().contiguous()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shape",
+    [
+        (1, 1, 8, 8, 4),
+        (1, 1, 17, 20, 32),
+        (1, 2, 8, 10, 8),
+    ],
+)
+def test_flux3_video_qknorm_rope_matches_eager(shape):
+    b, t, h, w, heads = shape
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    qkv = torch.randn(b, t, h, w, 3, heads, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    cos, sin = _tables(t, h, w, qkv.device)
+    assert can_use_flux3_video_qknorm_rope(qkv, cos, sin)
+    got = flux3_video_qknorm_rope(qkv, cos, sin, eps=_EPS)
+    ref = _reference(qkv, cos, sin)
+    for name, actual, expected in zip(("q", "k", "v"), got, ref):
+        assert torch.equal(actual, expected), name
+
+
+def test_natten_prepare_qkv_matches_eager_and_reuses_rope_cache():
+    _VIDEO_QKV_GATE.disabled = False
+    _VIDEO_QKV_GATE.verified = False
+    torch.manual_seed(1)
+    block = (
+        Natten3D(256, [5, 5, 5], num_heads=4, causal=True, qk_norm=True)
+        .cuda()
+        .bfloat16()
+        .eval()
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Muse Spark FP32 router logits (MuseSpark1xRouter): FP64 semantics, dispatch and graph state.
+
+Any-order FP32 dot products satisfy |fl(s) - s| <= gamma_K * sum_k |x_k w_k| plus an
+underflow term; small-integer inputs keep every partial sum exact, so any summation
+order must return the exact logits there. Decode-sized (T <= 8) FP32 inputs with
+16-byte aligned rows run the CuTe DSL GEMV on SM100-family GPUs (only T = 1 when TF32
+matmuls are allowed); everything else runs F.linear. Results are bitwise repeatable,
+including side-stream CUDA-graph replay.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl import (
+    MAX_TOKENS,
+    router_gemv_cute_eligible,
+)
+from sglang.srt.models.muse_spark import MuseSpark1xRouter
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+U = 2.0**-24
+
+
+def _router(w):
+    router = MuseSpark1xRouter(w.shape[1], w.shape[0], dtype=torch.float32).cuda()
+    router.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w, requires_grad=False)
+    return router
+
+
+def _inputs(tokens, hidden, experts, dist, pad=0, seed=0):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda")
+    g.manual_seed(seed)
+    if dist == "integer":
+        x = torch.randint(
+            -8, 9, (tokens, hidden + pad), generator=g, device="cuda"
+        ).float()
+        w = torch.randint(-8, 9, (experts, hidden), generator=g, device="cuda").float()
+    else:
+        x = torch.randn(tokens, hidden + pad, generator=g, device="cuda")
+        w = torch.randn(experts, hidden, generator=g, device="cuda") / hidden**0.5
+        if dist == "wide":
+            x = x * torch.exp2(
+                torch.randint(-30, 31, x.shape, generator=g, device="cuda").float()
+            )
+    return x[:, :hidden], w
+
+
+def _check(out, x, w, exact):
+    assert out.shape == (x.shape[0], w.shape[0]) and out.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert out.stride() == (w.shape[0], 1)
+    xd, wd = x.double(), w.double()
+    ref = xd @ wd.t()
+    k = x.shape[1]
+    bound = k * U / (1 - k * U) * (xd.abs() @ wd.abs().t()) + (2 * k + 1) * 2.0**-150
+    err = (out.double() - ref).abs()
+    if exact:
+        assert torch.equal(out.double(), ref)
+    else:
+        assert bool((err <= bound).all()), float((err / bound).max())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dist", ["normal", "wide", "integer"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pad", [0, 4, 3])
+def test_router_logits_semantics(tokens, dist, pad):
+    x, w = _inputs(tokens, 8192, 256, dist, pad, seed=tokens * 31 + pad)
+    router = _router(w)
+    before = (x.clone(), w.clone())
+    eligible = router_gemv_cute_eligible(x, w)
+    sm100 = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] == 10
+    assert torch.get_float32_matmul_precision() == "highest"
+    assert eligible == (sm100 and tokens <= MAX_TOKENS and pad % 4 == 0)
+    out = router(x)
+    out2 = router(x)
+    _check(out, x, w, dist == "integer")
+    assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int32), out2.view(torch.int32))
+    assert torch.equal(before[0], x) and torch.equal(before[1], w)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hidden,experts", [(2048, 64), (4096, 128), (1024, 32)])
+def test_router_logits_other_shapes(hidden, experts):
+    for tokens in (1, 4, 8):
+        x, w = _inputs(tokens, hidden, experts, "integer", seed=hidden + tokens)
+        _check(_router(w)(x), x, w, True)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 8])
+def test_router_side_stream_graph_replay(tokens):
+    x, w = _inputs(tokens, 8192, 256, "normal", seed=tokens)
+    router = _router(w)
+    sources = [
+        _inputs(tokens, 8192, 256, "normal", seed=100 + i)[0].contiguous()
+        for i in range(3)
+    ]
+    expected = [router(s).clone() for s in sources]
+    src = sources[0].clone()
+    main = torch.cuda.current_stream()
+    capture, side = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
+    capture.wait_stream(main)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=capture):
+        x.copy_(src)
+        side.wait_stream(capture)
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            out = router(x)
+        capture.wait_stream(side)
+    for rep in range(30):
+        src.copy_(sources[rep % 3])
+        out.fill_(float("nan"))
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int32), expected[rep % 3].view(torch.int32))
+
+
+def test_router_tf32_precision_keeps_multi_row_on_cublas():
+    """With TF32 matmuls allowed (the server default), only single-row logits move."""
+    sm100 = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] == 10
+    previous = torch.get_float32_matmul_precision()
+    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")
+    try:
+        for tokens in (1, 2, 8):
+            x, w = _inputs(tokens, 8192, 256, "integer", seed=tokens)
+            assert router_gemv_cute_eligible(x, w) == (sm100 and tokens == 1)
+            if tokens == 1:
+                _check(_router(w)(x), x, w, True)
+    finally:
+        torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(previous)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

+    from sglang.test.layer_ut_utils import init_single_process_dist
+
+    # Probe on all addresses: a port free on 127.0.0.1 can be busy on another
+    # local address (an active connection), and the store binds them all.
+    for attempt in range(6):
+        with socket.socket() as sock:
+            sock.bind(("", 0))

+def _pool(stack: int, k: int, width: int, seed: int):
+    """Dense pool slots as the memory pool writes them, stale past the rank."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+    a = torch.randn(SLOTS, stack * POOL_RANK, k, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 100
+    b = torch.randn(SLOTS, width, POOL_RANK, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 100
+    for slot, rank in enumerate(RANKS):
+        a[slot, : stack * rank] = (
+            torch.randn(stack * rank, k, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 0.05
+        )
+        b[slot, :, :rank] = torch.randn(width, rank, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 0.05
+    return a.to(DTYPE).contiguous(), b.to(DTYPE).contiguous()
+
+
+def _batch(seq_lens, slots, decode: bool):
+    seg_lens = torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    fb = SimpleNamespace(
+        forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE if decode else ForwardMode.EXTEND,
+        batch_size=len(seq_lens),
+        extend_seq_lens=seg_lens,
+        extend_seq_lens_cpu=list(seq_lens),
+        extend_num_tokens=int(sum(seq_lens)),
+        spec_info=None,
+        return_logprob=False,
+        extend_logprob_start_lens_cpu=None,
+    )
+    return fb, list(slots), list(RANKS), list(SCALINGS)

+def _layers(kind: str):
+    from sglang.srt.layers.linear import (
+        ColumnParallelLinear,
+        MergedColumnParallelLinear,
+        QKVParallelLinear,

+    from sglang.srt.lora.layers import get_lora_layer

+    common = dict(bias=False, params_dtype=DTYPE)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("request_capacity", [None, 48])
+def test_prefill_graph_admits_any_request_count_within_the_token_bucket(
+    request_capacity,
+):
+    """Replay ragged requests with the captured bucket's plan and route storage."""
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.lora.common.routing import _aligned_route_capacity
+    from sglang.srt.lora.dense.plan import DensePlan
+
+    wrap_row, k_row = _layers("row")
+    ours = TritonV2LoRABackend(SLOTS, DEVICE)
+    ours.init_prefill_cuda_graph_batch_info(512, request_capacity)
+    assert ours.prefill_cuda_graph_max_bs == (request_capacity or 512)
+    table = _TokensPlanTable(
+        DensePlan(block_size=32), DensePlan(block_size=16), threshold=128
+    )
+    ours.runner._plan_tables[POOL_RANK] = table
+    layer = wrap_row(ours)
+    bucket = 256
+    x = torch.randn(bucket, k_row, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)
+    out = torch.empty(
+        bucket, layer.base_layer.weight.shape[0], device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE
+    )
+
+    def forward():
+        ours.reset_routing_cache()
+        out.copy_(layer(x)[0])
+
+    def route_buffers(route):
+        # The route pads per slot, so its capacity ignores the request count.
+        assert (
+            bucket
+            <= route.sorted_pair_ids.numel()
+            <= _aligned_route_capacity(bucket, route.block_size, SLOTS)
+        )
+        ids = route.sorted_pair_ids[: route.num_pairs_post_padded.item()]
+        valid_ids = ids[(ids >= 0) & (ids < bucket)]
+        active_tokens = torch.where(ours.runner.token_slots >= 0)[0]
+        assert torch.isin(active_tokens, valid_ids).all().item()
+        return (
+            route.sorted_pair_ids.data_ptr(),
+            route.sorted_pair_ids.numel(),
+            route.block_bucket_ids.data_ptr(),
+        )
+
+    capture = _batch([bucket], [1], decode=False)
+    _prepare(ours, capture, use_prefill_cuda_graph=True)
+    assert not ours.runner.workspace.routes
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        forward()
+        warmup_route = ours.runner.route(table.large.block_size)
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    key = ("sorted", table.large.block_size, SLOTS)
+    assert _cached_route_keys(ours.runner) == {key}
+    buffers = route_buffers(warmup_route)
+    _prepare(ours, capture, use_prefill_cuda_graph=True)
+    assert not ours.runner.workspace.routes
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+        forward()
+        captured_route = ours.runner.route(table.large.block_size)
+    assert _cached_route_keys(ours.runner) == {key}
+
+    legacy = TritonLoRABackend(SLOTS, DEVICE)
+    seq_lens = [
+        1 + (i * 7) % 9 for i in range(48)
+    ]  # 48 ragged requests, 1..9 tokens each
+    slots = [(i * 3) % SLOTS for i in range(48)]
+    live = sum(seq_lens)
+    assert len(seq_lens) > 32 and live <= bucket
+    for batch in (
+        _batch(seq_lens, slots, decode=False),
+        _batch([90, 70, 50, 30], [2, 0, 3, 1], decode=False),
+        _batch([60, 40], [3, 0], decode=False),
+    ):
+        live = batch[0].extend_num_tokens
+        x.copy_(torch.randn_like(x))
+        _prepare(ours, batch, use_prefill_cuda_graph=True)
+        assert ours.runner.token_slots.numel() == live
+        assert not ours.runner.workspace.routes
+        captured_route.sorted_pair_ids.fill_(-7)
+        captured_route.block_bucket_ids.fill_(-7)
+        captured_route.num_pairs_post_padded.zero_()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert route_buffers(captured_route) == buffers
+        _prepare(legacy, batch)
+        expected = wrap_row(legacy)(x[:live])[0]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out[:live], expected, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+    _prepare(ours, batch)
+    site = (DenseLoraKind.LINEAR, POOL_RANK, k_row, layer.base_layer.weight.shape[0])
+    eager = ours.runner.plan_for(*site, num_tokens=live)
+    assert eager.block_size != captured_route.block_size

+class _TokensPlanTable:
+    def __init__(self, large, small, threshold):
+        self.large, self.small, self.threshold = large, small, threshold
+        self.queries = []
+
+    def plan_for(self, kind, phase, num_tokens, *geometry):
+        self.queries.append(num_tokens)
+        return self.large if num_tokens > self.threshold else self.small

+def test_variable_bucket_graphs_replay_without_dense_host_work(monkeypatch, prefill):
+    """Old graphs read refreshed metadata without Python planning or routing.
+
+    Each graph holds a qkv and a row site, and capture rebuilds the warm-up
+    route exactly once, inside the graph.
+    """
+    from sglang.srt.lora.dense.plan import DensePlan
+
+    wrap_qkv, k_qkv = _layers("qkv")
+    wrap_row, k_row = _layers("row")
+    ours = TritonV2LoRABackend(SLOTS, DEVICE)
+    table = _TokensPlanTable(
+        DensePlan(block_size=32),
+        DensePlan(block_size=16),
+        threshold=16,
+    )
+    ours.runner._plan_tables[POOL_RANK] = table
+    if prefill:
+        ours.init_prefill_cuda_graph_batch_info(64)
+    else:
+        ours.init_decode_cuda_graph_batch_info(64, 1)
+    layer_qkv, layer_row = wrap_qkv(ours), wrap_row(ours)
+    x_qkv = torch.randn(64, k_qkv, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)
+    x_row = torch.randn(64, k_row, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)
+    out_qkv = torch.empty(
+        64, layer_qkv.base_layer.weight.shape[0], device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE
+    )
+    out_row = torch.empty(
+        64, layer_row.base_layer.weight.shape[0], device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE
+    )
+    build_route = ours.runner._build_route
+    builds = []  # per route build: was the current stream capturing?
+
+    def counted_build(*args, **kwargs):
+        builds.append(torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing())
+        return build_route(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ours.runner, "_build_route", counted_build)
+
+    def batch_for(live, offset):
+        lengths = [live // 2, live - live // 2] if prefill else [1] * live
+        slots = [(i + offset) % SLOTS for i in range(len(lengths))]
+        return _batch(lengths, slots, decode=not prefill)
+
+    def prepare(batch):
+        _prepare(ours, batch, not prefill, use_prefill_cuda_graph=prefill)
+
+    graphs = {}
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()  # one stream for every bucket, as in a graph runner
+    for bucket in (64, 16):
+
+        def forward(bucket=bucket):
+            ours.reset_routing_cache()
+            out_qkv[:bucket].copy_(layer_qkv(x_qkv[:bucket])[0])
+            out_row[:bucket].copy_(layer_row(x_row[:bucket])[0])
+
+        queries = len(table.queries)
+        prepare(batch_for(11, 0))
+        assert len(table.queries) == queries
+        assert ours.runner._token_slots.numel() == 64
+        assert ours.runner.token_slots.numel() == 11
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            forward()
+            forward()
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+        count = len(builds)
+        graphs[bucket] = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graphs[bucket], stream=stream):
+            forward()
+        # The warm-up route is rebuilt exactly once, inside the capture.
+        assert builds[count:] == [True]
+        assert ours.runner._token_slots.numel() == 64
+        assert ours.runner.token_slots.numel() == bucket
+        plan = table.large if bucket > table.threshold else table.small
+        assert _cached_route_keys(ours.runner) == {("sorted", plan.block_size, SLOTS)}
+    assert table.queries == [64] * 6 + [16] * 6  # one plan per site per forward
+
+    def unexpected_dense_work(*args, **kwargs):
+        pytest.fail("preparation and replay must not plan or build dense routes")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ours.runner, "plan_for", unexpected_dense_work)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ours.runner, "_build_route", unexpected_dense_work)
+    legacy = TritonLoRABackend(SLOTS, DEVICE)
+    # The same local size can replay either bucket, including DP-wide padding.
+    for offset, (live, bucket) in enumerate(
+        ((11, 64), (11, 16), (40, 64), (16, 16), (64, 64))
+    ):
+        x_qkv.copy_(torch.randn_like(x_qkv))
+        x_row.copy_(torch.randn_like(x_row))
+        batch = batch_for(live, offset + 1)
+        prepare(batch)
+        assert ours.runner.token_slots.numel() == live
+        assert not ours.runner.workspace.routes
+        graphs[bucket].replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert not ours.runner.workspace.routes
+        _prepare(legacy, batch)
+        expected_qkv = wrap_qkv(legacy)(x_qkv[:live])[0]
+        expected_row = wrap_row(legacy)(x_row[:live])[0]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out_qkv[:live], expected_qkv, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out_row[:live], expected_row, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)

+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("verify", [False, True])
+def test_graph_phases_replay_with_changed_ranks_scales_and_old_buckets(verify):

+                    bridge.float() @ layer.B_buffer[slot, :, :rank].float().T

+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            output[:bucket].float(), expected, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

+"""Expand geometry caching and graph lifetime."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.lora.common.lora_b import (
+    grouped_lora_b,
+    slice_geometry,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.lora.common.route_view import RouteViewKind
+from sglang.kernels.ops.lora.common.routing import build_route
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+DEVICE = torch.device("cuda")
+DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
+SLOTS, RANK = 4, 32
+CONFIG = {
+    "BLOCK_SIZE_N": 64,
+    "BLOCK_SIZE_K": 32,
+    "GROUP_SIZE_M": 8,
+    "num_warps": 4,
+    "num_stages": 3,
+}
+TOL = dict(rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+
+
+def _site(offsets, tokens=41, seed=3):
+    """A ranked expand over ``offsets`` with a torch reference."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+    token_slots = torch.tensor(
+        [i % (SLOTS + 1) - 1 for i in range(tokens)], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    ranks = torch.tensor([32, 16, 8, 32], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    scalings = torch.tensor([1.5, 0.5, 2.0, 1.0], dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
+    slices = len(offsets) - 1
+    bridge = (torch.randn(tokens, slices * RANK, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 0.5).to(
+        DTYPE
+    )
+    weight = (
+        torch.randn(SLOTS, offsets[-1], RANK, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 0.05
+    ).to(DTYPE)
+    base = torch.randn(tokens, offsets[-1], generator=g, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)
+    route = build_route(
+        token_slots, max_loras=SLOTS, block_size=16, view=RouteViewKind.ALIGNED
+    )
+    expected = base.float().clone()
+    for t in range(tokens):
+        s = int(token_slots[t])
+        if s < 0:
+            continue
+        r = int(ranks[s])
+        for k in range(slices):
+            # slice k of a rank-r slot sits at bridge columns [k*r, (k+1)*r)
+            lo, hi = offsets[k], offsets[k + 1]
+            expected[t, lo:hi] += float(scalings[s]) * (
+                weight[s, lo:hi, :r].float() @ bridge[t, k * r : (k + 1) * r].float()
+            )
+    return (
+        dict(
+            bridge=bridge,
+            weight=weight,
+            base=base,
+            route=route,
+            ranks=ranks,
+            scalings=scalings,
+        ),
+        expected,
+    )
+
+
+def _expand(site, geometry, out):
+    grouped_lora_b(
+        site["bridge"],
+        site["weight"],
+        out,
+        site["route"],
+        geometry=geometry,
+        config=CONFIG,
+        add_inplace=True,
+        zero_sentinel=False,
+        lora_ranks=site["ranks"],
+        scalings=site["scalings"],
+    )
+
+
+def test_cache_normalizes_device_and_keeps_distinct_destination_columns():
+    rows = (0, 96, 192)
+    same = slice_geometry(rows, 64, DEVICE)
+    indexed = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
+    assert slice_geometry(rows, 64, indexed, out_offsets=rows[:-1]) is same
+    gapped = slice_geometry(rows, 64, indexed, out_offsets=(0, 128))
+    assert gapped is not same
+    assert gapped.out_offsets.tolist() == [0, 128] and same.out_offsets.tolist() == [
+        0,
+        96,
+    ]
+
+
+def test_a_captured_graph_keeps_its_tables_when_other_geometries_appear():
+    offsets = (0, 96, 224, 304)
+    site, expected = _site(offsets, seed=11)
+    geometry = slice_geometry(offsets, 64, DEVICE)
+    out = site["base"].clone()
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        _expand(site, geometry, out)  # warm-up compiles the kernel
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    out.copy_(site["base"])
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+        _expand(site, geometry, out)
+    del geometry  # Only the cache retains the tables after capture.
+    for i in range(3):
+        slice_geometry(
+            (0, 128 + 16 * (i + 1), 256 + 32 * (i + 1)), 64, DEVICE
+        )  # new entries after capture
+        out.copy_(site["base"])
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out.float(), expected, **TOL)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
